questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to choose a country that I found interesting, and I wanted to study in a bigger city. 
Besides, I wanted to study at a good university that had interesting courses that I could take. 
I also chose an English speaking country to improve my English and to ensure that my courses were internationally relevant.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Very good on a personal and social level. 
A bit of trouble with housing and other logistic aspects e.g., help/ with/information on credit transfer and such. 
Overall, very good experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I found that it was not very readily available online, both with housing (independent from the university) and with the university as well, for instance about how many credits I would need to be a full time student, and whether I was accepted to my classes or not. 
The UofT websites are quite confusing, even with a login. 

Before the arrival, I had issues with applying for on-campus residence, which I originally wanted to do. 
A lot of information was restricted for me, and the one e-mail contact did not reply before the deadline.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The exchange student coordinator Andrew is very kind, and was helpful when I e-mailed him with questions. 
Besides this, there was not a lot of assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I could have needed a bit more information and guidance from both my home and destination university, e.g., an overview of deadlines and links etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very hard to find housing. 
I lived at Harrington Housing Sherbourne, which I would not recommend. Very expensive and bad conditions.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
If at all possible, it is very worth it to find roommates (perhaps from your home country) to find an apartment with. 
In Toronto, housing is extremely expensive, no matter what, so it might be worth it to rent long term AirBnB (or similar) because it is more regulated/safe than renting "independently" from a person that could be scamming you financially or with bad housing conditions. 
A lot of student housing places are okay, but also expensive and have bad communication/conditions. 

Renting off campus is also a trade off where you will have more independence and possibly meet more people than people from your school, but living on-campus can also create a stronger bond with your fellow students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I don't quite remember the specifics, but my login came in an email, and I made an online appointment to get my student ID, which was easy to do. 
I registered for classes online as well, which I remember was a bit more tricky, but also fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had an e-mail to our coordinator Andrew.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not that succesful. Two of my top three choices were not created - I got in to two of my five choices. 
I had to find additional classes, which took a while to get accepted, even after the classes had started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make a document with all the information in the many e-mails/other contact information you have received beforehand, and don't be afraid to e-mail all of them, if you're not sure which one is the right for you to contact. 
This way, you will find a contact you can ask questions to if you have problems with registration. 
Don't be afraid to reach out to other exchange students in real life or online, or even regular students who might know where the physical office is located.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two third year courses which was my major (economics), and one course at 1 year level at another, closely related major (political science).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Mostly similar, but some differences. 
There is more contact between the professor and students, which might be because the classes were smaller. 
There is more debate at UofT than UCPH, which I appreciated. 
The curriculums felt a bit scattered. 
Grading at UofT also differs a lot, which I did not necessarily appreciate. 

I did not like the teaching style of the tutorials as much, and it is strange that our tutorial tutor is not the TA - the ones who teach us are not the ones who grade us, which makes it complicated when getting and understanding feedback on essays.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECO302H5
ECO335H5
POL115H5

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I will recommend ECO335H5. 
It is a small class which allows for more questions. Very interesting and relevant course with materials that updated every week.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Very expensive to have a phone number and data (300DKK). 
Taxes on every purchase as well as culturally mandatory tips. 
A lot of processing fees when paying with an international card, both in person and online. 
High living costs. 

It is important to be aware of changing exchange rates as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
More expensive: housing, phone bill, transportation, groceries. 
Nothing was less expensive than expected except maybe Starbucks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not dissatisfied, but I did not make use of any of these opportunities. I did not find them very available, but I can't rate any of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I believe there were many, but I am not sure as I didn't attend any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I have no recommendations specifically, but I would recommend joining one to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Montreal and Banff. Traveling is a bit expensive, but worth it with friends, since you get to experience more of the country. 
Taking one-day hikes is also great for bonding and getting a break from the city. 
I personally believe that it is more worth it to spend more on a vacation some weekends, and then doing less expensive activities (like a dinner party) other weekends rather than many restaurants etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The culture is not very different. The hardest part was getting used to the amount of homelessness.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Talk to the people in your class. 
However, I mostly socialized with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The social culture at the university is different, and it is harder to get into as an exchange student.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The outgoing, friendly attitudes of the Canadians. 
The culturally inclusivity as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Consider whether you want to live downtown, even if your campus is Scarborough or Mississauga - there are more opportunity/life there, but there is also travel time. 
Attend the first couple of events for exchange students, and don't be afraid to reach out during and after - other exchange students also don't know anybody and are looking for friends. 
Ask the local students what they do for fun/what is worth to do. 
In Canada the night life is quite different, but it is fun wherever the students are - they know the best places and are very open to include you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I did experience a lot of personal development and have made life-long friends. 
Having to figure out everything on my own and succeeding is also a very rewarding feeling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The logistical aspects, before, during and after the exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
